「なにしろ彼は新人なんだから、許してあげよう」他___是新来的，原谅他吧。: "He's new, after all, so let's forgive him." 「他___是新来的，原谅他吧。」
本質・事実を強調して理解を求めるのは「毕竟」。: Emphasizing the essence of something or a fact to ask for understanding is 「毕竟」.
「毕竟＋事実」で理由づけをします。: 「毕竟」 + fact is used to give a reason.
「幸亏」は「幸いにも〜だったので（悪い結果を免れた）」を表します。後半に「要不然: 「幸亏」 means "luckily, ... (so a bad outcome was avoided)." The second half is often followed by 「要不然・不然・否则」 ("otherwise") to show the bad outcome that was avoided. It corresponds to English "luckily," "it's a good thing ...," or "thank goodness ..."
言ってくれて助かった、でなければ忘れるところだった。: Good thing you reminded me; otherwise I would have forgotten.
「幸亏」はすでに起きたよい偶然・条件に使います。後半に「才」を使うと「〜だったか: 「幸亏」 is used for a fortunate chance or condition that has already happened. Using 「才」 in the second half gives "it was only because ... that ... was possible."
「早めに家を出てよかった、でなければ遅刻していた」___早出门了，不然就迟到了。: "Good thing I left home early; otherwise I would have been late." 「___早出门了，不然就迟到了。」
悪い結果を免れたのは「幸亏」。: Avoiding a bad outcome is 「幸亏」.
「幸亏…」の後半によく使われる語は？: Which word is often used in the second half of a 「幸亏…」 sentence?
免れた結果を「要不然・不然」で示します。: The outcome that was avoided is shown with 「要不然・不然」.
「难怪」は、理由がわかって「道理で〜なわけだ」と納得する気持ちを表します。理由を: 「难怪」 expresses the feeling of understanding something once you know the reason: "no wonder ..." It is often used together with 「原来」 ("so that's why / so it was ..."), which gives the reason. In speech, 「怪不得」 means almost the same thing.
道理で彼はあんなにうれしそうなわけだ、大学に受かったのか。: No wonder he's so happy; it turns out he got into college.
「难怪」は「理由がわかって納得」。ただ驚くだけなら「竟然」。「难怪」と「原来」を: 「难怪」 means "understanding once you know the reason." For simple surprise, use 「竟然」. Learn 「难怪」 and 「原来」 as a set.
「道理で暑いわけだ、エアコンが壊れていたのか」___这么热，原来空调坏了。: "No wonder it's so hot; the air conditioner is broken." 「___这么热，原来空调坏了。」
理由がわかって納得するのは「难怪」。: Understanding once you know the reason is 「难怪」.
「难怪」とほぼ同じ意味の口語表現は？: Which colloquial expression means almost the same as 「难怪」?
「除非」は「〜でない限り・〜してはじめて」と、唯一の条件を示します。「除非A，否: 「除非」 presents the one and only condition: "unless ... / only if ..." 「除非A，否则B」 means "unless A, B will happen," and 「除非A，才B」 means "only if A will B happen." Note that the condition after 「除非」 is written in the affirmative, just as after English "unless" (not "unless it doesn't ...").
大雨が降らない限り、試合は予定どおり行われる。: Unless it rains heavily, the match will go ahead as usual.
×除非不下雨 → 「雨が降らない限り」でも「除非下雨，否则…（雨が降らなければ…: ×「除非不下雨」 → To say "unless it rains," think of it in the structure 「除非下雨，否则…」 ("unless it rains; if it doesn't, ..."), with no negative after 「除非」. It's close in meaning to 「只有…才…」.
「病気でない限り、彼は欠席しない」___生病，否则他不会请假。: "Unless he's sick, he won't miss it." 「___生病，否则他不会请假。」
唯一の条件は「除非…否则…」。: The one and only condition is 「除非…否则…」.
「除非…，才…」に近い表現は？: Which expression is close to 「除非…，才…」?
唯一の条件を表す「只有…才…」と近い意味です。: It's close in meaning to 「只有…才…」, which also expresses the one and only condition.
「要不是」は「もし〜でなかったら」と、実際に起きた事実を仮に否定して、起こり得た: 「要不是」 means "if it weren't (for) ...," hypothetically negating something that actually happened and describing the different outcome that could have happened (「要不是你帮忙，我就完不成了」). What follows is the actual fact, so it is stated in the affirmative, not with 「不」. It often expresses gratitude or regret.
あなたが手伝ってくれなかったら、私一人では絶対に終わらなかった。: If you hadn't helped, I definitely couldn't have finished on my own.
「要是…（もし〜なら）」は単純な仮定、「要不是…」は事実の裏返し。×要不是你不帮: 「要是…」 ("if ...") is a simple hypothetical, while 「要不是…」 flips a fact. Be careful not to make a double negative like ×「要不是你不帮忙」.
「雨が降らなかったら試合は中止にならなかった」___下雨，比赛就不会取消了。: "If it hadn't rained, the match wouldn't have been canceled." 「___下雨，比赛就不会取消了。」
事実を仮に否定するのは「要不是」。: Hypothetically negating a fact is 「要不是」.
「要不是你来了」が表す事実は？: What actually happened in 「要不是你来了」?
「要不是＋事実」なので、実際には来ています。: It's 「要不是」 + fact, so the person actually did come.
「一方面…另一方面…」一方では〜、他方では…: 「一方面…另一方面…」: on the one hand ..., on the other hand ...
「一方面…另一方面…」は、ある物事の2つの側面や2つの理由を並べて述べる表現です: 「一方面…另一方面…」 lays out two aspects of something, or two reasons, side by side. It is handy in essays and speeches for organizing reasons or contrasting pros and cons. The second half is often accompanied by 「也」 or 「又」.
中国語を学ぶのは、一つは仕事に必要だから、もう一つは中国文化が好きだからだ。: I study Chinese partly because I need it for work and partly because I like Chinese culture.
後半は「一方面」の繰り返しではなく「另一方面」とするのが正式です。理由を述べる文: The proper form for the second half is 「另一方面」, not a repeat of 「一方面」. In sentences giving reasons, combining it with 「是因为」 makes things neat.
「一方面…」に続く後半の決まった言い方は？: What is the set phrase for the second half after 「一方面…」?
「一方面…另一方面…」がセットです。: 「一方面…另一方面…」 is a set.
この表現が最も適しているのは？: When is this expression most appropriate?
2つの側面・理由を並べるとき: When listing two aspects or reasons
2つの側面を並べる表現です。: It's an expression for laying out two aspects side by side.
「A不如B」AはBに及ばない: 「A不如B」: A is not as good as B
「A不如B」は「AはBに及ばない・Bのほうがいい」を表す比較の表現です。後ろに形: 「A不如B」 is a comparison meaning "A is not as good as B / B is better." With an adjective after it, it means "A is not as ... as B" (「坐公交不如坐地铁快」). The adjective is basically one with a positive meaning, and it's more formal than 「没有…那么」. It's the same 「不如」 as in 「与其…不如…」.
私の中国語は彼ほど上手ではない。: My Chinese isn't as good as his.
×今天不如昨天冷 のように否定的な形容詞は避け、「今天没有昨天冷」とするのが自然: Avoid negative adjectives, as in ×「今天不如昨天冷」; 「今天没有昨天冷」 is natural. 「不如」 is usually used with positive words such as 「好・快・方便」.
「私は兄ほど背が高くない」として自然なのは？: Which is natural for "I'm not as tall as my older brother"?
「电话不如见面。」の意味は？: What does 「电话不如见面。」 mean?
電話より会うほうがいい: Meeting in person is better than calling
会うより電話のほうがいい: Calling is better than meeting in person
電話も会うのも同じ: Calling and meeting are the same
「A不如B」＝AはBに及ばない（Bがよい）。: 「A不如B」 = A is not as good as B (B is better).
「简直」は「まったく・まるで〜と言ってもいいほどだ」と、やや大げさに程度を強調す: 「简直」 is an adverb that emphasizes degree with some exaggeration: "simply / practically / you could almost say ..." In patterns such as 「简直是…」, 「简直像…一样」, and 「简直太…了」, it expresses surprise, admiration, or annoyance. It feels close to English "simply," "practically," or "unbelievably."
ここの景色は本当に美しすぎる！: The scenery here is simply gorgeous!
「简直」は事実より大げさに言う感覚。単に「とても」なら「非常」で十分です。「简单: 「简直」 has the sense of saying more than the plain facts. If you just mean "very," 「非常」 is enough. Be careful, since it looks similar to 「简单」 ("simple").
「まるで夢のようだ」___像做梦一样。: "It's just like a dream." 「___像做梦一样。」
「趁」は「〜のうちに・〜の機会を利用して」と、条件や時機をうまく利用して何かをす: 「趁」 means "while ... / taking advantage of the opportunity of ...," showing that you make good use of a condition or timing to do something (「趁热吃」 = "eat it while it's hot"). It can be followed by a noun, an adjective, or a verb phrase. It corresponds well to English "while (it's still) ..." and can also be said as 「趁着」.
餃子は熱いうちに食べてね。: Eat the dumplings while they're hot.
「趁」の後ろは「よい機会・条件」。「〜しないうちに」も「趁＋否定」で表せます（趁: What follows 「趁」 is a good opportunity or condition. "Before ... happens" can also be expressed with 「趁」 + negative (「趁他还没来」).
「若いうちにもっと勉強しよう」として正しいのは？: Which is correct for "Let's study more while we're young"?
「从…来看」は「〜（の観点・資料）から見ると」と、判断の根拠や立場を示す表現です: 「从…来看」 means "judging from (a viewpoint or data) ...," showing the basis or standpoint for a judgment. It's used as in 「从目前的情况来看」 ("judging from the current situation") and 「从这一点来看」 ("from this point of view"), followed by a judgment or conclusion. 「看来」 and 「来说」 are also used, but 「来看」 is the usual choice for stating a basis.
現状から見ると、問題はそれほど深刻ではない。: Judging from the current situation, the problem isn't very serious.
「对…来说（〜にとって）」は立場、「从…来看（〜から見ると）」は根拠・観点。似て: 「对…来说」 ("for ...") is about standpoint, while 「从…来看」 ("judging from ...") is about basis or viewpoint. They're similar, but use them appropriately.
「調査結果から見ると、多くの人が賛成している」___调查结果来看，很多人都同意。: "Judging from the survey results, many people agree." 「___调查结果来看，很多人都同意。」
根拠・観点は「从…来看」。: A basis or viewpoint is 「从…来看」.
「〜にとって」を表すのはどれ？: Which one means "for ..." (as far as someone is concerned)?
「偏偏」あいにく・よりによって: 「偏偏」: of all times, just has to
「偏偏」は「あいにく・よりによって」と、期待や都合に反することが起こった不満を表: 「偏偏」 means "unfortunately / of all times," expressing frustration that something happened contrary to one's hopes or convenience (「我要出门，偏偏下雨了」). It also means a person deliberately goes against something, "insists on ... / just has to ..." (「不让他去，他偏偏要去」). Both carry the speaker's dissatisfaction or irritation.
ちょうど出かけようとしたら、あいにく雨が降り出した。: Just as I was about to go out, it had to start raining.
「偏偏」には話し手の不満が含まれるので、うれしい偶然には使いません。うれしい偶然: 「偏偏」 carries the speaker's dissatisfaction, so it isn't used for happy coincidences. For a happy coincidence, use 「正好・恰好」 ("just right / as it happens").
「急いでいるのに、よりによってバスが来ない」我很着急，公共汽车___不来。: "I'm in a hurry, and of all times the bus won't come." 「我很着急，公共汽车___不来。」
期待に反する事態は「偏偏」。: A situation contrary to expectations is 「偏偏」.
うれしい偶然「ちょうど」を表すのは？: Which one expresses a happy coincidence, "just right / as it happens"?
「恨不得」は「〜できないのが恨めしい→〜したくてたまらない」という強い願望を表し: 「恨不得」 expresses a strong wish: "it's frustrating that I can't ... → I'm dying to ..." It is mostly used for exaggerated wishes that can't actually come true (「恨不得马上飞回家」). It is close to English "I wish I could ... right now," "be dying to ...," or "can't wait to ..." There is no negative form, and note that despite the character 「恨」, it carries no meaning of anger.
その良い知らせを聞いて、彼は今すぐみんなに伝えたくてたまらなかった。: When he heard the good news, he couldn't wait to tell everyone right away.
「恨不得」の後ろには「马上・立刻・一下子」などの「すぐに」を表す語がよく来ます。: 「恨不得」 is often followed by words meaning "right away," such as 「马上・立刻・一下子」. Understand 「恨」 here not as "hate / resent" but as "frustrated (at being unable to)."
「今すぐ休暇に入りたくてたまらない。」我___马上放假。: "I'm dying for the vacation to start right now." 「我___马上放假。」
強い願望は「恨不得」。「舍不得」は「名残惜しい」。: A strong wish is 「恨不得」. 「舍不得」 means "hate to part with / reluctant to let go."
「恨不得」の説明として正しいのは？: Which explanation of 「恨不得」 is correct?
〜するしかないという意味。: It means "have no choice but to ..."
実現困難な強い願望を表す。: It expresses a strong wish that's hard to fulfill.
怒りではなく、強い願望を表します。: It expresses not anger but a strong wish.
「有的是」は「たくさんある・いくらでもある」と数量が十分に多いことを強調する話し: 「有的是」 is a colloquial expression stressing that there is more than enough of something: "there's plenty / no end of ..." The 「的是」 part is for emphasis, and note that it has a completely different meaning from 「有些是」 ("some are ..."). It's close to English "there's plenty of ..." or "there's no shortage of ...," and is often used to reassure someone or tell them not to hold back.
焦らないで、時間はいくらでもあるから。: Don't worry, we've got plenty of time.
「有的是」は「yǒudeshì」と一語で読み、「多い」の意味。「有的…有的…（あ: 「有的是」 is read as one word, 「yǒudeshì」, and means "a lot." Don't confuse it with 「有的…有的…」 ("some ..., others ...").
彼はお金をいくらでも持っている。: He has more money than he knows what to do with.
彼のお金は一部だけだ。: He has only part of the money.
「有的是」は数量が非常に多いことを強調します。: 「有的是」 stresses a very large quantity.
「依然」「仍然」は「状況が変わっても、以前と同じ状態が続いている」ことを表す副詞: 「依然」 and 「仍然」 are adverbs showing that "even though circumstances have changed, the same state as before continues." They are written-style versions of 「还是」 and correspond to English "still" or "as ever." They are often preceded by a contrastive word such as 「虽然」 or 「尽管」, emphasizing the contrast that nothing changed even though something else did.
何年もたったが、ここは依然として静かだ。: Although many years have passed, it's still very quiet here.
「依然」は形容詞の前に「是」なしで置けます（依然很美）。「仍然」は動詞の前によく: 「依然」 can go before an adjective without 「是」 (「依然很美」). 「仍然」 is often used before verbs.
「何度説明しても、彼は相変わらず分からなかった。」解释了好几遍，他___不明白。: "No matter how many times I explained, he still didn't understand." 「解释了好几遍，他___不明白。」
状態が変わらないことは「依然」。: A state that doesn't change is 「依然」.
「仍然」に最も意味が近い話し言葉の語は？: Which colloquial word is closest in meaning to 「仍然」?
「仍然」は「还是（やはり・依然として）」の書き言葉です。: 「仍然」 is the written-style version of 「还是」 ("still").
「再…不过了」は「これ以上〜なものはない＝最高に〜だ」という最上級の強調表現です: 「再…不过了」 is an emphatic superlative meaning "nothing could be more ... = as ... as it gets." The adjective is sandwiched between 「再」 and 「不过了」, as in 「再好不过了」 and 「再合适不过了」. It corresponds to English "couldn't be better / couldn't be more ..." and is mostly used for positive evaluations. It's often used in everyday conversation to say "that would be perfect."
手伝いに来てくれるなら、それに越したことはない。: If you can come and help, that would be perfect.
形容詞は「再」と「不过」の間に入れます（×再不过好了）。文末の「了」もセットです: The adjective goes between 「再」 and 「不过」 (×「再不过好了」). The 「了」 at the end is also part of the set.
「再＋形容詞＋不过了」の語順です。: The word order is 「再」 + adjective + 「不过了」.
「再…不过了」の意味として正しいのは？: Which is the correct meaning of 「再…不过了」?
「明明」は「明らかに〜なのに」と、はっきりした事実を示し、それに反する言動や結果: 「明明」 is an adverb that points to a clear fact, "clearly ... (and yet)," expressing dissatisfaction or puzzlement at words, actions, or results that contradict it. It is typically followed by 「可是」, 「却」, 「怎么」, 「为什么」, etc. It's close to English "I definitely ..., so why ..." or "it's obvious that ..., but ...," and is often used to blame someone or express that you can't accept something.
確かにカギを机の上に置いたのに、どうして見つからないんだろう。: I definitely put the keys on the table, so why can't I find them?
「明明」の後半には逆接（却／可是）や疑問（怎么／为什么）が来ることが多いです。単: The second half of a 「明明」 sentence often has a contrast (「却／可是」) or a question (「怎么／为什么」). If you just want to say "it's obvious," use 「很明显」.
「確かに見たのに、彼はないと言う。」我___看见了，他却说没有。: "I definitely saw it, but he says there wasn't one." 「我___看见了，他却说没有。」
事実に反する言動への不満は「明明」。: Dissatisfaction with words or actions that contradict a fact is 「明明」.
「明明」の後ろに最も続きやすいのは？: What is most likely to follow 「明明」?
矛盾を示す「却・可是」などが続きます。: Words showing a contradiction, such as 「却・可是」, follow.
「好在」は「良くない状況の中で、幸いにも〜という有利な条件がある」ことを表す副詞: 「好在」 is an adverb meaning "in a bad situation, fortunately there is the favorable condition that ..." Typically the first half describes the trouble, and 「好在」 comes at the beginning of the second half. It's similar to 「幸亏」, but while 「幸亏」 focuses on the result, "thanks to ..., a bad outcome was avoided," 「好在」 points to the saving condition itself.
雨がひどく降っていたが、幸い傘を持っていた。: It was raining hard, but fortunately I had brought an umbrella.
「好在」は後半の文頭に置きます。「幸亏」は「幸亏…，不然…」の形がよく使われます: 「好在」 goes at the beginning of the second half. 「幸亏」 is often used in the pattern 「幸亏…，不然…」, but 「好在」 doesn't take such a fixed follow-up.
「財布をなくしたが、幸い中にお金はあまりなかった。」钱包丢了，___里面钱不多。: "I lost my wallet, but fortunately there wasn't much money in it." 「钱包丢了，___里面钱不多。」
救いとなる条件を示すのは「好在」。: Pointing to a saving condition is 「好在」.
「偏偏」と「好在」の関係として正しいのは？: Which correctly describes the relationship between 「偏偏」 and 「好在」?
「偏偏」は不運、「好在」は幸運を表し、意味が反対に近いです。: 「偏偏」 expresses bad luck and 「好在」 good luck; they're nearly opposite in meaning.
「万一」万が一・もしも: 「万一」: in case, if by any chance
「万一」は「可能性は低いが、もしも〜したら」と、起こってほしくない事態を仮定する: 「万一」 is a conjunction that supposes an unwanted situation: "it's unlikely, but if by any chance ..." It is close to English "in case" or "if by some chance," and is followed by a countermeasure or worry. Unlike 「如果」, it's characteristically used only for bad situations. As a noun, it also appears in the set phrase 「以防万一」 ("just in case").
万が一雨が降ったら、別の日に行こう。: If by any chance it rains, we'll go another day.
「万一」は良いことの仮定には使いません（×万一中奖了）。良いことなら「如果・要是: 「万一」 isn't used to suppose good things (×「万一中奖了」). For good things, use 「如果・要是」.
「万が一遅れたら、先に行っていて。」___我迟到了，你们就先走。: "If by any chance I'm late, go on ahead." 「___我迟到了，你们就先走。」
悪い事態の仮定は「万一」。: Supposing a bad situation is 「万一」.
「万一」の使い方として不自然なのは？: Which use of 「万一」 is unnatural?
「万一」は望ましくない事態の仮定に使います。: 「万一」 is used to suppose undesirable situations.
「再说」は理由を一つ挙げたあと、「それに〜でもあるし」とさらに理由を追加する話し: 「再说」 is a colloquial conjunction that adds another reason after one has been given: "besides, ... too." It's close to English "besides" or "what's more," and is often used when turning down a suggestion or reinforcing an opinion. As a verb it also means "think about it later / put it off" (「以后再说」), so tell the two apart by context.
今日はもう遅いし、それに私も疲れたから、明日行こう。: It's too late today, and besides, I'm tired; let's go tomorrow.
「再说」は理由の追加。「以后再说／回头再说」は「あとで考えよう」という先送りの決: 「再说」 adds a reason. 「以后再说／回头再说」 is a set phrase for putting something off: "let's think about it later."
「遠いし、それに道もよく知らない。」太远了，___我也不认识路。: "It's too far, and besides, I don't know the way." 「太远了，___我也不认识路。」
「等考完试再说。」の意味は？: What does 「等考完试再说。」 mean?
試験が終わったらもう一度言う。: I'll say it again after the exam.
試験が終わってから考えよう。: Let's think about it after the exam.
試験のことは言わない。: I won't say anything about the exam.
「再说」は「あとで考える」という先送りの意味にもなります。: 「再说」 can also mean putting something off, "think about it later."
「不至于」〜するほどではない・まさか〜まではしない: 「不至于」: not to the point of ..., surely won't go so far as to ...
「不至于」は「ある程度にまでは達しない」、つまり「まさか〜ほどにはならないだろう: 「不至于」 means "doesn't reach a certain degree," that is, a negative guess about an extreme outcome: "surely it won't get to the point of ..." It's close to English "it won't come to that" or "surely ... won't go so far as to ..." The affirmative 「至于」 is rarely used on its own in this sense; it appears in rhetorical questions such as 「至于吗？」 ("Is that really necessary?").
彼は怒ったけれど、君を無視するほどではないだろう。: He got angry, but not to the point of ignoring you.
「不至于」は程度の否定的推測。話題転換の「至于（〜については）」とは別の用法なの: 「不至于」 is a negative guess about degree. It's a different use from topic-changing 「至于」 ("as for ..."), so keep them apart.
「少し遅れても、怒られるほどではないだろう。」晚到几分钟，___被批评吧。: "Even if you're a few minutes late, surely you won't get scolded for it." 「晚到几分钟，___被批评吧。」
「〜するほどではない」は「不至于」。: "Not to the point of ..." is 「不至于」.
「为这点事吵架，至于吗？」の意味は？: What does 「为这点事吵架，至于吗？」 mean?
この件で喧嘩するのは当然だ。: Fighting over this is only natural.
この件で喧嘩するほどのこと？: Is this really worth fighting over?
「至于吗？」は「そこまでする？」という反語です。: 「至于吗？」 is a rhetorical question meaning "Is that really necessary? / Do you have to go that far?"
「好像…似的」まるで〜のようだ: 「好像…似的」: just like, as if
「似的（shìde）」は文末につけて「〜のようだ」という比喩や推測を表す助詞で、: 「似的」 (shìde) is a particle placed at the end of a phrase to express a comparison or guess, "it's like ...," and is often combined with 「好像」 or 「像」 in the pattern 「好像…似的」. It corresponds to English "just like ..." or "as if ..." It means almost the same as 「像…一样」, but 「似的」 is more colloquial and can wrap a whole verb phrase as is, so it's often used to describe how someone looks or behaves.
彼はまるで子どものように喜んでいる。: He's as happy as a child.
「似的」は「sìde」ではなく「shìde」と読みます。「好像」だけでも意味は通: 「似的」 is read 「shìde」, not 「sìde」. 「好像」 alone gets the meaning across, but adding 「似的」 strengthens the sense of comparison.
「彼はまるで病気のように顔色が悪い。」他脸色很差，好像生病了___。: "He looks terrible, as if he were sick." 「他脸色很差，好像生病了___。」
「好像…似的」で「まるで〜のようだ」。: 「好像…似的」 means "just like / as if."
「似的」の読み方として正しいのは？: What is the correct pronunciation of 「似的」?
介詞の「作为」は「〜として」と、ある身分・立場・資格から何かをすることを表します: As a preposition, 「作为」 means "as" and shows that someone acts from a certain role, position or capacity (「作为老师」 = as a teacher). It often comes at the start of the sentence, and the subject that follows is the same person or thing as the noun after 「作为」. As a verb, it is also used in the form 「把A作为B」 ("to take A as B").
学生として、いちばん大切なのは勉強だ。: As a student, the most important thing is studying.
「作为」の後ろは身分や資格を表す名詞です。「〜として扱う・〜とみなす」と言いたい: What follows 「作为」 is a noun for a role or capacity. To say "treat as" or "regard as," you can also use the more colloquial 「把A当作B」 or 「把A当成B」 (see the 「当作」 entry).
「医者として、患者の健康を第一に考えるべきだ。」___医生，应该把病人的健康放在: "As a doctor, you should put patients' health first." 「___医生，应该把病人的健康放在第一位。」
身分・立場「〜として」は「作为」。: A role or position, "as ...," is 「作为」.
「作为」＋身分を表す名詞で「〜として」となります。: 「作为」 + a noun for a role means "as ...".
「把A当作／当成B」AをBとみなす・AをBと間違える: 「把A当作/当成B」: treat A as B, mistake A for B
「把A当作B」「把A当成B」は「AをBとみなす・AをBとして扱う」という意味です: 「把A当作B」 and 「把A当成B」 mean "to regard A as B" or "to treat A as B." They are used both when someone really treats A that way, as in 「把我当成朋友」 ("think of me as a friend"), and for mistakes, as in 「把盐当成了糖」 ("mistook salt for sugar"). In speech, 「拿A当B」 is also used. This 「当」 is read dàng, with the fourth tone.
彼はずっと私を本当の妹のように思ってくれている。: He has always treated me like his own little sister.
「当作」「当成」の「当」は「dàng」（〜とみなす）で、「当时」「应当」の「dā: The 「当」 in 「当作」 and 「当成」 is dàng ("to regard as"), unlike the dāng in 「当时」 and 「应当」. Since it is a 「把」 sentence, A must be a specific person or thing.
「彼はいつも私を子ども扱いする。」他总是把我___孩子。: "He always treats me like a child." 「他总是把我___孩子。」
「我把他当成了他哥哥。」の意味は？: What does 「我把他当成了他哥哥。」 mean?
彼を兄として紹介した。: I introduced him as my older brother.
彼を彼の兄と間違えた。: I mistook him for his older brother.
彼の兄を頼りにした。: I relied on his older brother.
「把A当成了B」は「AをBと間違えた」という勘違いにもよく使います。: 「把A当成了B」 is often used for mistakes: "mistook A for B."
「在…下」は「〜のもとで・〜を受けて」と、ある条件や他者の働きかけの下で何かが起: 「在…下」 means "under" or "with" and shows that something happens under certain conditions or thanks to someone else's influence. Typically a two-syllable noun goes in the middle, such as 「帮助」 (help), 「支持」 (support), 「影响」 (influence), 「指导」 (guidance) or 「情况」 (circumstances). It comes at the start, and the result follows in the second half.
先生の助けのおかげで、無事に試験に合格した。: With my teacher's help, I passed the exam without any trouble.
「下」を忘れて×「在老师的帮助，…」としないこと。「〜の面で」は「在…上」（「在: Don't forget 「下」 (×「在老师的帮助，…」). There are set pairings: 「在…上」 for "in terms of" (「在工作上」 = in terms of work) and 「在…中」 for "in the course of."
「医者の指導のもとで、彼は毎日運動している。」在医生的指导___，他每天都运动。: "Under his doctor's guidance, he exercises every day." 「在医生的指导___，他每天都运动。」
「指导」「帮助」「影响」などは「在…下」と組みます。: Words like 「指导」, 「帮助」 and 「影响」 go with 「在…下」.
「在…下」の間に入る語として最も自然なのは？: Which word fits most naturally inside 「在…下」?
「在…的帮助下」（〜の助けのもとで）が典型的な形です。: 「在…的帮助下」 ("with the help of ...") is the typical form.
「好不容易（才）」やっとのことで: 「好不容易（才）」: with great difficulty, finally
「好不容易」は「やっとのことで・苦労してようやく」という意味で、後ろに「才」を伴: 「好不容易」 means "with great difficulty" or "finally, after a lot of trouble," and is often followed by 「才」. Before a verb, 「好容易」 means exactly the same thing; with or without 「不」, both describe something that was finally achieved. As a predicate, however, they keep their literal meanings: 「好不容易」 = "very difficult," 「好容易」 = "very easy."
やっとのことでこの切符を手に入れた。: I finally managed to get this ticket after a lot of trouble.
動詞の前の「好不容易」「好容易」はどちらも「やっとのことで」です。まずは「好不容: Before a verb, both 「好不容易」 and 「好容易」 mean "with great difficulty." Learn the form 「好不容易」 + 「才」 + verb first and you won't go wrong.
「やっとのことで駅に着いた。」我们___才到车站。: "We finally made it to the station." 「我们___才到车站。」
「我好容易才找到工作。」の意味は？: What does 「我好容易才找到工作。」 mean?
やっとのことで仕事が見つかった。: I finally found a job after a lot of trouble.
仕事を見つけるのは簡単だ。: It's easy to find a job.
動詞の前の「好容易」は「好不容易」と同じく「やっとのことで」です。: Before a verb, 「好容易」 means the same as 「好不容易」: "with great difficulty."
「直到…才…」は「〜になってやっと…した」と、ある時点まで実現しなかったことがよ: 「直到…才…」 means "not until ... did ...": something that didn't happen up to a certain point finally happened. 「才」 adds the feeling that it was late. With a negative or 「还」 in the second half, as in 「直到现在」, it means "even now, still ...". 「直到…为止」 means "(all the way) until ...".
夜中になってようやく彼は帰ってきた。: He didn't come home until midnight.
「才」は「就」と逆で「遅い・やっと」の気持ちを表します。「直到…才」の文では、ふ: 「才」 is the opposite of 「就」 and conveys "late, only then." Sentences with 「直到…才」 usually don't take 「了」 at the end.
「夜の11時になってようやく仕事が終わった。」___晚上十一点，我___下班。: "I didn't get off work until 11 p.m." 「___晚上十一点，我___下班。」
「直到今天，我还不知道他的名字。」の意味は？: What does 「直到今天，我还不知道他的名字。」 mean?
今日になっても彼の名前をまだ知らない。: Even today, I still don't know his name.
今日まで彼の名前を知っていた。: I knew his name until today.
今日やっと彼の名前を知った。: I finally learned his name today.
後半が「还不…」なので、「〜になってもまだ…ない」です。: The second half is 「还不…」, so it means "even ..., still not ...".
「就算…也…」は「たとえ〜としても…」と仮定の譲歩を表す話し言葉の表現で、「即使: 「就算…也…」 means "even if ..., (still) ..." and expresses a hypothetical concession. It is colloquial and means almost the same as 「即使…也」. The form 「就算是…」 is also common. In writing, 「即使」 and 「即便」 are more common; in speech, 「就算」 and 「哪怕」. Don't leave out 「也」 in the second half.
たとえ言わなくても、わかっているよ。: Even if you don't say it, I know.
「就算」は仮定、「虽然」は事実の逆接です。実際に雨が降っているなら「虽然下雨，但: 「就算」 is for hypotheticals; 「虽然」 is for facts. If it is actually raining, say 「虽然下雨，但是…」; if you don't know whether it will rain, say 「就算下雨，也…」.
「たとえお金があっても、そんな高い物は買わない。」___有钱，我___不买那么贵: "Even if I had the money, I wouldn't buy something that expensive." 「___有钱，我___不买那么贵的东西。」
「就算」に最も意味が近いのは？: Which is closest in meaning to 「就算」?
「就算」は「即使」の話し言葉的な言い方です。: 「就算」 is a colloquial equivalent of 「即使」.
「要么A，要么B」は「Aするか、さもなければBするか（どちらか一つ）」と、二つの: 「要么A，要么B」 means "either A or B (one or the other)" and shows that you have to choose one of two options. It is often used when making a proposal or pushing for a decision, and usually takes verb phrases. It carries a stronger sense than 「或者」 of "you have to pick one."
君が来るか、僕が行くか、どちらにせよ一度会わなきゃ。: Either you come here or I go there; we have to meet up at some point.
「要么」は選択を迫る言い方で、疑問文の「AかBか」には「还是」を使います（「你喝: 「要么」 is for forcing a choice. In questions asking "A or B?", use 「还是」 (「你喝茶还是咖啡？」).
「タクシーで行くか、地下鉄で行くか、どちらかだ。」___打车去，___坐地铁去。: "We either take a taxi or take the subway." 「___打车去，___坐地铁去。」
二者択一の「〜か…か」は「要么…要么…」。: "Either ... or ..." between two options is 「要么…要么…」.
「要么」＋動詞句を二つ並べて、どちらかを選ばせます。: Two 「要么」 + verb phrase clauses set out the choice.
「V来V去」〜したり〜したり・あれこれ〜する: 「V来V去」: ... back and forth, ... over and over
同じ動詞を「来」と「去」の前に繰り返すと、「行ったり来たり〜する」「何度も繰り返: Repeating the same verb before 「来」 and 「去」 means "... back and forth" or "... over and over." Besides real movement back and forth, as in 「走来走去」 ("pace up and down"), it is often followed by the conclusion reached after all that repetition, as in 「想来想去」 ("after thinking it over and over") and 「说来说去」 ("when all is said and done").
彼は入り口を行ったり来たりしていて、焦っているようだ。: He's pacing back and forth at the door; he seems anxious.
「来」が先、「去」が後です（×「走去走来」）。方向だけを表す「走来」「走去」とは: 「来」 comes first and 「去」 second (×「走去走来」). Unlike 「走来」 or 「走去」, which only show direction, this pattern means repetition.
「あれこれ選んだ末、結局一番安いのを買った。」我___，最后买了最便宜的。: "After going back and forth, I ended up buying the cheapest one." 「我___，最后买了最便宜的。」
動詞＋「来」＋動詞＋「去」の語順です。: The order is verb + 「来」 + verb + 「去」.
飛び回る・行ったり来たりする: fly around, fly back and forth
「V来V去」は往復や繰り返しを表します。: 「V来V去」 expresses back-and-forth movement or repetition.
副詞の「白」は「無駄に・むなしく」を表し、努力や行動が報われなかったことを言いま: The adverb 「白」 means "in vain" and says that an effort or action came to nothing (「白跑一趟」 = make a wasted trip). It can also mean "for free, without paying" (「白吃白喝」 = eat and drink for free). In both meanings it goes before the verb.
店が閉まっていて、無駄足を踏んだ。: The store was closed, so our trip was wasted.
「白」は色の「白い」だけではありません。「白费」（無駄にする）、「白白地」（むざ: 「白」 doesn't only mean the color white. 「白费」 ("to waste") and 「白白地」 ("for nothing") belong to the same family. In the "for free" sense, 「白吃」 has a slightly negative ring of "without paying for it."
「書類を忘れて、無駄足を踏んだ。」我忘了带材料，___跑了一趟。: "I forgot the documents, so the trip was wasted." 「我忘了带材料，___跑了一趟。」
動詞の前の「白」は「ただで」や「無駄に」の意味です。: 「白」 before a verb means "for free" or "in vain."
「的确」と「确实」はどちらも「確かに・本当に」と、事実であることを認めたり強調し: 「的确」 and 「确实」 are both adverbs meaning "indeed" or "really," used to acknowledge or stress that something is true. They are also common when agreeing with someone (「的确如此」 = that's exactly right). The difference is that 「确实」 can also be an adjective, as in 「确实的消息」 ("reliable information") and 「消息很确实」, while 「的确」 can only be an adverb.
「的确」の「的」は「dí」と読みます（「目的」の「的」と同じ）。「确实的消息」は: The 「的」 in 「的确」 is read dí (as in 「目的」). You can say 「确实的消息」, but not ×「的确的消息」.
「その情報はあまり確かではない。」这个消息不太___。: "That information isn't very reliable." 「这个消息不太___。」
形容詞として述語になれるのは「确实」だけです。: Only 「确实」 can serve as an adjective predicate.
「的确」について正しいのは？: Which statement about 「的确」 is correct?
形容詞として名詞を修飾できる: It can modify nouns as an adjective.
副詞として「確かに」の意味で使う: It is used as an adverb meaning "indeed."
否定文には使えない: It can't be used in negative sentences.
「的确」は副詞専用で、「的」は「dí」と読みます。: 「的确」 is only an adverb, and its 「的」 is read dí.
「之」は古典由来の助詞で、現代では書き言葉や決まった言い方で「的」の代わりに使わ: 「之」 is a particle of Classical origin, used today in place of 「的」 in written style and set expressions (「原因之一」 = "one of the reasons"). It also appears in fractions, as in 「三分之一」 ("one third"), and in many words such as 「之前・之后・之间・总之」, making it essential for HSK 6 reading.
これは私の大好きな都市の一つです。: This is one of my favorite cities.
分数は日本語と同じく分母が先：3分の1＝三分之一。「〜の一つ」は「之一」で、前に: In fractions, unlike English, the denominator comes first: "one third" = 「三分之一」. "One of ..." is 「之一」, and it must always be preceded by a group of several (such as 「最…的作家」).
「彼は中国で最も有名な作家の一人だ。」他是中国最有名的作家___。: "He is one of China's most famous writers." 「他是中国最有名的作家___。」
「5分の2」を中国語で言うと？: How do you say "two fifths" in Chinese?
分母が先で「五分之二」。: The denominator comes first: 「五分之二」.
「以」は書き言葉で「〜を用いて・〜で」（以优惠的价格出售＝特価で販売する）、「〜: In written style, 「以」 means "using / with" (「以优惠的价格出售」 = "sold at a special price") or "by." When it follows a previous clause as 「…，以」 + verb, it expresses purpose, "in order to ...," and this is the same 「以」 as in 「以便」 and 「以免」. You see it all the time in ads and notices.
私たちは最速で現場に駆けつけた。: We rushed to the scene as fast as we could.
「八折」は「定価の8割＝2割引」。日本語の「8割引」と逆なので要注意！「以＋価格: 「八折」 means "80% of the list price = 20% off." Be careful not to read it as "80% off"! 「以」 + price/method + 「出售」 is a standard expression in ads.
「彼は優秀な成績で卒業した。」他___优异的成绩毕业了。: "He graduated with excellent grades." 「他___优异的成绩毕业了。」
「八折」は定価の8割で売る＝2割引。: 「八折」 means selling at 80% of the list price = 20% off.
「乃至」さらには・ひいては: 「乃至」: and even, and by extension
「乃至」は「さらには・ひいては」の意味で、範囲がだんだん広がる列挙の最後に置き、: 「乃至」 means "and even / and by extension." It goes at the end of a list whose scope gradually widens, introducing the largest item. It's more formal than 「甚至」 and suited to emphasizing how far the scope extends. Note that it does not mean "A or B" or "anywhere from A to B."
この発見は中国、ひいては世界全体にとって重要な意味を持つ。: This discovery is significant for China and even for the whole world.
日本語の「AないしB」（AまたはB）とは別物。中国語の「乃至」は「さらには」で、: It does not mean "A or B." Chinese 「乃至」 means "and even," with the scope getting larger toward the end.
「この問題は地域、ひいては国全体に関わる。」这个问题关系到地方___整个国家。: "This issue concerns the region, and by extension the entire country." 「这个问题关系到地方___整个国家。」
中国語の「乃至」の意味に最も近いのは？: Which is closest to the meaning of 「乃至」 in Chinese?
「乃至」は「さらには・ひいては」。: 「乃至」 means "and even / and by extension."
「鉴于」は「〜という状況を考慮して・〜に鑑みて」という意味の硬い書き言葉で、公式: 「鉴于」 is a stiff written-style expression meaning "considering the situation that ... / in view of ...," used in official documents, notices, business documents, and so on. The first half presents the situation, and the second half states the judgment or measure based on it. It can be used much like English "in view of" or "in light of."
天候を考慮し、試合は来週に延期します。: Due to the weather, the match has been postponed until next week.
「由于」は単なる原因、「鉴于」は「それを踏まえて判断・対応する」というニュアンス: 「由于」 is simply a cause, while 「鉴于」 has the nuance of "making a judgment or responding based on that." It sounds natural with a response such as 「决定」 or 「需要」 in the second half.
「申込者が多いことを考慮し、会場を変更します。」___报名人数较多，我们决定更换: "In view of the large number of applicants, we will change the venue." 「___报名人数较多，我们决定更换会场。」
状況を踏まえて措置を述べるのは「鉴于」。: Stating a measure based on a situation is 「鉴于」.
「鉴于」が最もよく使われる場面は？: In what situation is 「鉴于」 most often used?
「况且」は「それに・しかも」と、すでに述べた理由にさらに理由を付け加えるときに使: 「况且」 means "besides / moreover," used to add another reason to one already given. It's often followed by 「又」, 「也」, or 「还」. In speech, 「再说」 does almost the same job. 「何况」 is mainly used for the inference "let alone ..."
今日はもう遅いし、それに外は雨だから、明日にしよう。: It's too late today, and besides, it's raining outside; let's go tomorrow.
理由を並べて結論を補強するなら「况且」。「何况…呢？」（ましてや）の反語的な推論: To line up reasons that support a conclusion, use 「况且」. Keep it distinct from the rhetorical inference of 「何况…呢？」 ("let alone").
「この部屋は駅に近いし、それに家賃も安い。」这个房子离车站近，___房租也便宜。: "This apartment is close to the station, and besides, the rent is cheap." 「这个房子离车站近，___房租也便宜。」
「况且」とほぼ同じ意味の話し言葉は？: Which colloquial word means almost the same as 「况且」?
「固然」は「確かに〜ではあるが」と、まず一方の事実を認めたうえで、後半で別の観点: 「固然」 means "admittedly / it's true that ...," first acknowledging one fact and then presenting another point of view in the second half. 「固然…但是…」 concedes and then counters (「钱固然重要，但健康更重要」), while 「固然…也…」 accepts both (「去固然好，不去也行」). It's more argumentative than 「虽然」 and is often used in essays and opinion pieces.
お金は確かに大切だが、健康の方がもっと大切だ。: Money is certainly important, but health is more important.
「固然」は副詞なので主語の後ろに置きます（×固然钱重要 → 钱固然重要）。主語の: 「固然」 is an adverb, so it goes after the subject (×「固然钱重要」 → 「钱固然重要」). Note the difference from 「虽然」, which can also go before the subject.
「固然」は主語の後ろ、述語の前。: 「固然」 goes after the subject and before the predicate.
「才能も確かに大事だが、努力の方がもっと大事だ。」天赋___重要，但努力更重要。: "Talent is certainly important, but effort is more important." 「天赋___重要，但努力更重要。」
一方を認めて反論するのは「固然…但…」。: Conceding one point and then countering is 「固然…但…」.
「倘若」「假如」はどちらも「もし〜ならば」で、「如果」の書き言葉的な言い方です。: 「倘若」 and 「假如」 both mean "if" and are written-style versions of 「如果」. 「倘若」 in particular appears in literature, opinion pieces, and formal documents. Besides 「就」, the second half may also pair with the written-style 「便」 or 「则」. 「假如」 is also often used for suppositions contrary to reality.
もし明日天気が悪ければ、イベントは日を改めて行う。: If the weather is bad tomorrow, the event will be rescheduled.
「倘若・假如・如果・要是」は硬さが違うだけでほぼ同じ意味。会話は「要是／如果」、: 「倘若・假如・如果・要是」 differ only in formality and mean almost the same thing. Use 「要是／如果」 in conversation; using 「倘若／假如」 in essays and emails makes them crisper.
「如果」と最も意味が近い書き言葉は？: Which written-style word is closest in meaning to 「如果」?
「もし不明な点があれば、いつでもお問い合わせください。」___有不明白的地方，请: "If anything is unclear, please feel free to ask at any time." 「___有不明白的地方，请随时咨询。」
「未免」は「いささか〜すぎる・〜と言わざるをえない」と、ある状況に控えめな否定的: 「未免」 means "rather too ... / one can't help saying ...," giving a restrained negative evaluation of a situation (「你这么说未免太过分了」 = "Saying that is going a bit too far"). It is often used with 「太」, 「有点儿」, or 「过于」, and softens direct criticism.
そんなやり方は、いささか不公平すぎる。: Doing it this way is a bit too unfair.
「未免」＝やんわり批判、「难免」＝避けられない。字が似ていますが意味は別です。「: 「未免」 = gentle criticism, 「难免」 = unavoidable. They look similar but mean different things. Adding 「太・过于」 after 「未免」 sounds natural.
「たった一度の失敗であきらめるのは、いささか早すぎる。」只失败一次就放弃，___: "Giving up after failing just once is a bit too early." 「只失败一次就放弃，___太早了。」
控えめな批判「〜すぎる」は「未免」。: Restrained criticism, "a bit too ...," is 「未免」.
「未免」は「いささか〜すぎる」という評価。: 「未免」 is an evaluation meaning "a bit too ..."
反語「何尝」〜でないことがあろうか: Rhetorical 「何尝」: how could it not be ...?
「何尝」は書き言葉の反語で、「何尝不…」は「〜しないことがあろうか（実は〜してい: 「何尝」 is a written-style rhetorical question: 「何尝不…」 emphasizes the positive, "how could I not ...? (I actually do)," and 「何尝…」 emphasizes the negative, "when did I ever ...? (I didn't)." 「我何尝不想去」 means "It's not that I don't want to go (I really do)." It's used to clear up a misunderstanding or appeal to someone's feelings.
私だって休みたいよ、でも仕事が多すぎるんだ。: Don't you think I want to rest too? But there's just too much work.
「何尝不」＝実は肯定、「何尝」（否定なし）＝実は否定。反語は「肯定と否定が逆転す: 「何尝不」 = actually positive; 「何尝」 (with no negative) = actually negative. If you remember that rhetorical questions flip positive and negative, you can sort out 「难道」 and 「何必」 at the same time.
「我何尝不想回家？」の意味は？: What does 「我何尝不想回家？」 mean?
私は家に帰りたくない: I don't want to go home
私だって家に帰りたい: Of course I want to go home too
「何尝不…」は反語で肯定を強調します。: 「何尝不…」 is rhetorical and emphasizes the positive.
「私がいつ君をだましたというのか（だましていない）。」我___骗过你？: "When did I ever deceive you? (I didn't.)" 「我___骗过你？」
否定を強調する反語は「何尝」。: The rhetorical form emphasizing the negative is 「何尝」.
「务必」は「必ず・ぜひとも〜するように」と、相手に強く求める書き言葉です。通知や: 「务必」 is a written-style word that makes a strong request of someone: "be sure to / by all means ..." It's often used in notices and business emails in the form 「请务必…」 ("please be sure to ..."). It's similar to 「一定」, but 「务必」 is centered on making a request of someone and has no meaning of conjecture ("must surely be").
必ず金曜日までにレポートを提出してください。: Please be sure to submit your report by Friday.
「他一定知道（彼はきっと知っている）」のような推量に「务必」は使えません。相手へ: 「务必」 can't be used for conjecture such as 「他一定知道」 ("He must know"). Remember it as reserved for requests and instructions to others.
「必ず期限内にお支払いください。」请___在规定时间内付款。: "Please be sure to pay within the deadline." 「请___在规定时间内付款。」
「务必」が使えないのはどれ？: In which sentence can 「务必」 not be used?
推量「きっと〜だろう」は「一定」を使います。: For the conjecture "must surely be," use 「一定」.
「从而」は「それによって・その結果」と、前の行動や方法がもたらす結果を導く書き言: 「从而」 is a written-style conjunction meaning "thereby / as a result," introducing the result brought about by a previous action or method. The subject is basically the same in both halves, and the second half often has a positive result such as 「提高」, 「促进」, or 「实现」. While 「因此」 is simple cause and effect, 「从而」 emphasizes the link "method → achievement."
彼は勉強法を改善し、それによって成績を上げた。: He improved his study methods and thereby raised his grades.
「从而」の後ろには新しい主語を置かないのが原則です。作文では「通过…，从而…（〜: As a rule, no new subject is put after 「从而」. In essays, the pattern 「通过…，从而…」 ("through ..., thereby ...") is handy.
「毎日運動を続けたことで、体が丈夫になった。」他坚持每天运动，___增强了体质。: "By sticking to exercising every day, he became stronger." 「他坚持每天运动，___增强了体质。」
方法がもたらす結果は「从而」。: A result brought about by a method is 「从而」.
「从而」の後ろに来る内容として最も自然なのは？: What is most natural after 「从而」?
前の方法がもたらす結果: The result the preceding method brings about
「以便」〜しやすいように: 「以便」: so that, in order to
「以便」は「〜しやすいように・〜するために」と、前の行動の目的を後半で述べる書き: 「以便」 is written style meaning "so that ... can / in order to ...," stating the purpose of the earlier action in the second half. While 「以免」 means "to avoid a bad situation," 「以便」 means "to make a good goal easier to achieve." It's used following a previous clause and isn't placed at the start of a sentence.
ご連絡できるよう、電話番号を残してください。: Please leave your phone number so that we can contact you.
「以便」＝良い目的、「以免」＝悪い結果の回避。「以便迟到」は×（遅刻するために？: 「以便」 = a good purpose; 「以免」 = avoiding a bad result. 「以便迟到」 is × ("in order to be late"?) → 「以免迟到」. Choose based on whether what follows is good or bad.
「すぐ見つかるように、鍵は玄関に置いておく。」我把钥匙放在门口，___随时能找到: "I keep my keys by the front door so I can find them anytime." 「我把钥匙放在门口，___随时能找到。」
良い目的を実現しやすくするのは「以便」。: Making a good goal easier to achieve is 「以便」.
「忘れないようにメモしておく。」我把它记下来，___忘了。: "I'll write it down so I don't forget." 「我把它记下来，___忘了。」
悪い事態（忘れる）を避けるのは「以免」。: Avoiding a bad situation (forgetting) is 「以免」.
「与…相比」は「〜と比べると」という書き言葉の比較表現で、文頭に置いて比較の基準: 「与…相比」 is a written-style comparison meaning "compared with ...," placed at the start of a sentence to show the basis of comparison (「与去年相比，…」). The second half often has 「更」, 「比较」, or words showing an increase or decrease. In speech, people say 「和／跟…比起来」. It's a standard expression in reports and the news.
昨年と比べ、今年の観光客は20%増えた。: Compared with last year, the number of tourists this year rose by 20%.
「与其他方法相比」の「与其」は「与其…不如」とは無関係で、「与＋其他（ほかの）」: The 「与其」 in 「与其他方法相比」 has nothing to do with 「与其…不如」; it's 「与」 + 「其他」 ("other"). Be careful not to misread where the words break.
「先月と比べて、今月の売上は10%増えた。」___上个月相比，这个月的销售额增长: "Compared with last month, sales this month rose by 10%." 「___上个月相比，这个月的销售额增长了百分之十。」
「与…相比」で比較の基準を示します。: 「与…相比」 shows the basis of comparison.
「与…相比」の話し言葉の言い方は？: How do you say 「与…相比」 colloquially?
「莫非」は「もしかして〜なのではないか」と、意外な可能性を推測するときに使う書き: 「莫非」 is written style used to guess at an unexpected possibility: "could it be that ...?" It's similar to 「难道」, but while 「难道」 presses rhetorically, "surely it can't be ...," 「莫非」 has a stronger sense of guessing, "could it be ...?" 「不成」 or 「吗」 is sometimes added at the end.
彼が今日来ていないのは、もしかして病気なのでは？: He didn't come today; could he be sick?
「莫非」＝もしかして〜？（推測）、「难道」＝まさか〜じゃないだろうね（反語・詰問: 「莫非」 = "could it be ...?" (a guess); 「难道」 = "surely you don't mean ...?" (rhetorical, pressing). They often appear in dialogue in novels and dramas.
「電話に出ない。もしかして寝ちゃったのかな？」他不接电话，___睡着了？: "He's not answering the phone. Could he have fallen asleep?" 「他不接电话，___睡着了？」
意外な可能性の推測は「莫非」。: Guessing at an unexpected possibility is 「莫非」.
「莫非」に最も近い日本語は？: Which is closest in meaning to 「莫非」?
「莫非」は推測の「もしかして」。: 「莫非」 is the guessing "could it be ...?"
「可见」〜であることがわかる: 「可见」: it can be seen that ...
「可见」は「（このことから）〜であることがわかる」と、前に述べた事実や例から結論: 「可见」 means "(from this) it can be seen that ...," drawing a conclusion from facts or examples mentioned before. In essays and opinion pieces, summing up with 「由此可见」 ("from this we can see") after concrete examples is standard. It is followed by the speaker's judgment or conclusion.
彼は毎日遅くまで練習している。いかに真剣かがわかる。: He practices until late every day, which shows how serious he is.
「可见」は「見ることができる」ではなく「〜とわかる」。作文の結びに「由此可见，…: 「可见」 doesn't mean "can be seen (with the eyes)"; it means "it's clear that ..." Ending an essay with 「由此可见，…」 really tightens the logic.
「ここからわかるように、健康は何より大切だ。」由此___，健康比什么都重要。: "From this we can see that health matters more than anything." 「由此___，健康比什么都重要。」
「可见」は前の事実から結論を導きます。: 「可见」 draws a conclusion from the facts that come before.
「不料」は「ところが思いがけず〜」と、予想や期待に反することが起きたことを表す書: 「不料」 is an adverb leaning toward written style, expressing that something happened contrary to one's expectations or hopes: "but unexpectedly ..." Typically the first half states a plan or expectation, and 「不料」 comes at the start of the second half. It's close to English "but unexpectedly" or "to one's surprise," and is mostly used for unwelcome developments. In speech, 「没想到」 is more common.
週末は山登りに行くつもりだったが、思いがけず一日中雨が降った。: I'd planned to go hiking on the weekend, but unexpectedly it rained all day.
「不料」は文と文をつなぐ位置（後半の頭）に置くのが基本です。会話なら「没想到」に: 「不料」 basically goes in the position that links two clauses (the start of the second half). In conversation, it sounds natural to replace it with 「没想到」.
「出かけようとしたら、思いがけず客が来た。」刚要出门，___来了客人。: "Just as I was about to go out, a guest unexpectedly showed up." 「刚要出门，___来了客人。」
予想外の展開は「不料」。「果然」は予想どおり。: An unexpected development is 「不料」. 「果然」 means "as expected."
「不料」の話し言葉での言い換えとして最も近いのは？: Which is the closest colloquial replacement for 「不料」?
「势必」は「成り行きからして必ず〜になる」と、ある状況から避けられない結果を論理: 「势必」 is a written-style adverb that logically predicts an unavoidable result from a situation: "given how things are going, ... is bound to happen." It's a stiff expression close to English "inevitably" or "is bound to," often used in opinion pieces and reports. It describes the result of circumstances, not the speaker's will, so be careful not to confuse it with 「必须」 ("must").
すぐに対処しなければ、問題は必ずますます深刻になる。: If it isn't dealt with promptly, the problem is bound to get more and more serious.
「势必」は「成り行きで必ずそうなる」、「必须」は「義務としてそうしなければならな: 「势必」 means "will inevitably happen given how things are going," while 「必须」 means "must, as an obligation." ×「我势必完成作业」 → 「我必须完成作业」.
「人手が足りなければ、必然的に効率に影響する。」人手不够，___会影响效率。: "If we're short-handed, it will inevitably affect efficiency." 「人手不够，___会影响效率。」
状況から避けられない結果は「势必」。: An unavoidable result of a situation is 「势必」.
「势必」の意味として正しいのは？: Which is the correct meaning of 「势必」?
「务必」は依頼、「不必」は不要。「势必」は必然の結果。: 「务必」 is a request and 「不必」 means "no need." 「势必」 is an inevitable result.
「动不动就…」何かというとすぐ〜する: 「动不动就…」: at the slightest thing
「动不动就…」は「ちょっとしたことですぐ〜する」と、ある行為が頻繁に起きることを: 「动不动就…」 is a colloquial expression saying that an action happens frequently, "at the slightest thing ...," with a feeling of complaint or exasperation. It's close to English "at the drop of a hat" or "always ... at the slightest thing," and tends to go with undesirable actions such as 「发脾气・哭・请假」. Note that it's almost never used in praise.
彼は気が短くて、何かというとすぐ怒る。: He has a bad temper and blows up at the slightest thing.
「动不动就」は非難・不満の色が強い表現です。×他动不动就帮助别人（褒める文脈）は: 「动不动就」 carries a strong tone of criticism or complaint. ×「他动不动就帮助别人」 (in a context of praise) is unnatural; say 「他经常帮助别人」.
「彼は何かというとすぐ休みを取る。」他___请假。: "He takes time off at the slightest excuse." 「他___请假。」
頻繁で好ましくない行為には「动不动就」。: For frequent, undesirable actions, use 「动不动就」.
「动不动就」と最も相性がよい内容は？: What goes best with 「动不动就」?
不満を込める表現なので、好ましくない行為と結びつきます。: It's an expression of complaint, so it goes with undesirable actions.
「以至（于）」〜するほどまでに・その結果: 「以至（于）」: so much so that, to the point that
「以至（于）」は前の状況の程度が高いために「〜するほどにまでなった」と、行き着い: 「以至（于）」 is a written-style conjunction showing the result reached because the earlier situation was so extreme: "to the point that ..." It's close to English "so ... that ..." or "to the point that ..." The result is usually unwelcome. It is also written 「以致」, but that form is limited to even worse results. Don't confuse it with HSK 5's 「（不）至于」 ("not to the point of ...").
彼は仕事に没頭するあまり、食事をするのも忘れた。: He was so absorbed in his work that he forgot to eat.
「以至于」は前半の程度が原因で結果が生じる流れです。前半に「太・很・非常」など程: With 「以至于」, the result arises from the degree in the first half. It sounds natural when the first half has an intensifier such as 「太・很・非常」.
「彼は夢中になって読み、駅を乗り過ごすほどだった。」他看得太入迷了，___坐过了: "He was so engrossed in reading that he missed his stop." 「他看得太入迷了，___坐过了站。」
程度が高くて行き着いた結果は「以至于」。: A result reached because of a high degree is 「以至于」.
「以便」は目的、「至于」は話題転換。: 「以便」 is purpose and 「至于」 is a change of topic.
「不免」は前の状況から「自然と〜になってしまう、〜せずにはいられない」ことを表す: 「不免」 is an adverb showing that, given the preceding situation, "one naturally ends up ... / can't help but ..." Its meaning is close to HSK 5's 「难免」, but because 「不免」 is an adverb, it must always go before a verb or adjective; it can't go at the end of a sentence or be wrapped in 「是…的」. It's close to English "can't help ..." or "naturally end up ...," and is often used in sentences describing changes in feelings or state of mind.
こんな大勢の前で初めて話すので、どうしても少し緊張してしまう。: Speaking in front of so many people for the first time, I can't help feeling a little nervous.
×这是不免的 → 这是难免的。「不免」は副詞専用で、述語として使えるのは「难免」: ×「这是不免的」 → 「这是难免的」. 「不免」 is adverb-only; only 「难免」 can be used as a predicate.
「誤りは避けられないものだ。」として正しいのは？: Which is correct for "Mistakes are unavoidable"?
「〜是…的」で述語に使えるのは「难免」。: Only 「难免」 can be used as the predicate in 「〜是…的」.
「久しぶりに故郷に帰り、つい胸が高鳴った。」好久没回老家，心里___有些激动。: "Going back to my hometown after so long, I couldn't help feeling excited." 「好久没回老家，心里___有些激动。」
自然とそうなってしまう気持ちは「不免」。: A feeling that comes about naturally is 「不免」.
「进而」さらに進んで・その上で: 「进而」: and then go on to, and further
「进而」は「Aを達成したうえで、さらに一歩進んでBする」と、段階的に発展していく: 「进而」 is a written-style conjunction expressing step-by-step development: "having achieved A, go a step further and do B." It's close to English "and then go on to" or "and further," and is favored in proposals and opinion pieces. It differs from 「从而」 ("as a result"), which expresses a result, in that 「进而」 expresses moving forward to the next stage.
まず顧客のニーズを理解し、さらにサービスの質を高めなければならない。: We first need to understand our customers' needs, and then go on to improve the quality of our service.
「进而」はA→Bと段階が上がるイメージ。単なる結果なら「从而」、目的なら「以便」: 「进而」 gives the image of stepping up from A to B. For a simple result, use 「从而」; for a purpose, use 「以便」.
「まず基本を固め、さらに進んで応用を学ぶ。」先打好基础，___学习应用。: "First build a solid foundation, then go on to learn the applications." 「先打好基础，___学习应用。」
次の段階へ進むのは「进而」。: Moving on to the next stage is 「进而」.
「进而」と「从而」の違いとして正しいのは？: Which correctly describes the difference between 「进而」 and 「从而」?
「进而」は次の段階への前進、「从而」は結果: 「进而」 is moving on to the next stage; 「从而」 is a result
「进而」は前進、「从而」はそれによる結果。: 「进而」 means moving forward; 「从而」 means the result brought about by that.

「历来」は「昔から今までずっと」という意味の書き言葉の副詞で、長い期間変わらない: 「历来」 is a written-style adverb meaning "always, from long ago until now," expressing a tendency, tradition, or policy that has remained unchanged for a long time. It's similar to 「一向」, but while 「一向」 is often used for an individual's personality or habits, 「历来」 is often used to talk about larger scopes or long histories, such as countries, regions, organizations, or fields. It's close to English "has always" or "traditionally."
この地域は昔からおいしい料理で有名だ。: This place has long been famous for its food.
「历来」は長い歴史・伝統の継続に重点があります。個人の最近の習慣には「一向」「一: 「历来」 emphasizes the continuation of a long history or tradition. For an individual's recent habits, 「一向」 or 「一直」 is more natural.
「この町は昔から茶の産地として知られている。」这个小镇___以产茶闻名。: "This town has long been known for producing tea." 「这个小镇___以产茶闻名。」
「历来」と「一向」の違いとして最も適切なのは？: What is the most fitting difference between 「历来」 and 「一向」?
「历来」は未来、「一向」は過去を表す。: 「历来」 refers to the future and 「一向」 to the past.
「历来」は歴史・伝統など大きな範囲に使われやすい。: 「历来」 tends to be used for broad scopes like history and tradition.
「历来」は話し言葉専用である。: 「历来」 is used only in speech.
「历来」は書き言葉で、長い歴史や伝統によく使います。: 「历来」 is written style and is often used for long histories and traditions.
「诸如」は「例えば〜のような」といくつかの例を挙げる書き言葉の表現で、後ろに「等: 「诸如」 is a written-style expression for giving several examples, "such as ...," typically rounded off with 「等」 or 「之类」 after it to mean "... and the like." It's more formal than 「比如」 and is often used in reports and explanatory writing. It corresponds to English "such as ..." or "... and the like." Listing several examples is more natural than giving just one.
このような問題は、また後で話し合いましょう。: Issues like these we'll discuss later.
「诸如此类」は「このような類のもの」という四字成語として単独でもよく使います。: 「诸如此类」 ("things of this kind / and so on") is also often used on its own as a four-character idiom.
「書道や茶道といった伝統文化」___书法、茶艺之类的传统文化: "traditional culture such as calligraphy and the tea ceremony" 「___书法、茶艺之类的传统文化」
例を挙げる書き言葉は「诸如」。: The written-style word for giving examples is 「诸如」.
「诸如」の後ろで例をまとめる語として最も自然なのは？: Which word most naturally rounds off the examples after 「诸如」?
「诸如…之类／等」とまとめます。: Round it off as 「诸如…之类／等」.
「为…所…」は書き言葉の受け身で、「〜によって…される」を表します（「为人所知」: 「为…所…」 is a written passive meaning "be ...ed by ..." (「为人所知」 = be known to people). The agent goes after 「为」 and the verb after 「所」. The verb is usually two syllables, such as 「感动」, 「吸引」, 「接受」 or 「理解」, and the pattern often appears in idioms and set phrases. It corresponds to spoken 「被」 but sounds more formal and literary.
この秘密はとっくに人々に知られている。: This secret has long been known to people.
この「为」は「wéi」と読みます（「为了」の「wèi」とは別）。「所」を省いた「: This 「为」 is read wéi, not the wèi of 「为了」. There is also a form without 「所」 (「为」 + two-syllable verb), but learn the full 「为…所…」 set first.
「この作品は多くの読者に愛されている。」这部作品___广大读者___喜爱。: "This work is loved by a great many readers." 「这部作品___广大读者___喜爱。」
受け身の「为」は第2声の「wéi」です。: The passive 「为」 is wéi, with the second tone.
「加以」〜を加える・〜する（書き言葉）: 「加以」: to carry out, to give (formal)
「加以」は後ろに2音節の動詞を取り、「（その対象に）〜という処置を施す」ことを表: 「加以」 takes a two-syllable verb and means "to apply (a certain action) to something." It is a formal, written "dummy" verb: in 「加以分析」 ("to analyze") and 「加以解决」 ("to solve"), the real meaning is in the verb that follows. The target is shown with 「对…」 or by the context, and no object comes after 「加以」 + verb.
これらのデータについては、分析を加える必要がある。: We need to analyze this data.
×「加以分析数据」のように目的語を後ろに置くのは誤りで、「对数据加以分析」としま: Putting the object after it, as in ×「加以分析数据」, is wrong; say 「对数据加以分析」. A one-syllable verb can't follow it either (×「加以看」).
「この点については、もう少し説明を加える必要がある。」这一点还需要___说明。: "This point needs some more explanation." 「这一点还需要___说明。」
2音節動詞の前に置いて「〜を施す」を表すのは「加以」。: The word placed before a two-syllable verb to mean "apply ..." is 「加以」.
対象は「对…」で前に出し、「加以」＋2音節動詞で終えます。: Put the target first with 「对…」 and end with 「加以」 + a two-syllable verb.
「有所」は「いくらか〜するところがある・ある程度〜する」という意味の書き言葉で、: 「有所」 is a written expression meaning "to some extent" or "somewhat," followed by a two-syllable verb (「有所提高」 = has improved somewhat). It is handy for describing changes or degrees modestly and is common in reports and the news. There are many set combinations, such as 「有所不同」 ("somewhat different") and 「有所了解」 ("know something about").
1年の努力を経て、彼の成績はいくらか向上した。: After a year of hard work, his grades have improved somewhat.
「有所」の後ろは2音節の動詞です（×「有所好」→「有所好转」）。話し言葉なら「提: A two-syllable verb follows 「有所」 (×「有所好」→「有所好转」). In speech, you can rephrase it as 「提高了一些」.
「いくらか〜した」は「有所」＋2音節動詞。: "... somewhat" is 「有所」 + a two-syllable verb.
「切勿・不得」〜してはならない（掲示・規則の禁止）: 「切勿」「不得」: must not (notices and rules)
掲示や規則、注意書きでは、話し言葉の「别」「不要」の代わりに書き言葉の禁止表現を: Notices, rules and warnings use written prohibitions instead of spoken 「别」 or 「不要」. 「切勿」 is a strong warning or piece of advice, "never ...," as in 「切勿外传」 ("do not share this with others"). 「不得」 states that something "must not" be done under rules or laws, as in 「不得吸烟」 ("no smoking").
貴重品はお持ちください。決して車内に置いたままにしないでください。: Please keep your valuables with you and never leave them in the car.
「不得」は「〜できない」ではなく「〜してはならない」です。「不得不」（〜せざるを: 「不得」 means "must not," not "cannot." Don't confuse it with 「不得不」 ("have no choice but to"). Using 「切勿」 or 「不得」 in a chat with friends sounds overly formal.
「館内は撮影禁止です。」馆内___拍照。: "Photography is prohibited inside the building." 「馆内___拍照。」
規則による禁止は「不得」＋動詞。: A prohibition by rule is 「不得」 + verb.
「切勿」に最も近い話し言葉は？: Which spoken expression is closest to 「切勿」?
「切勿」は「千万别」（決して〜しないで）の書き言葉です。: 「切勿」 is the written counterpart of 「千万别」 ("whatever you do, don't").
「殊不知」ところが実は〜（思い込みを正す）: 「殊不知」: little do they know, but in fact
「殊不知」は「（そう思っているが）実は〜だということを知らない」という意味で、前: 「殊不知」 means "(they think so, but) little do they know that ...". The first half states a belief and the second half the actual fact, pointing out the mistake. It is a written expression, close to English "but in fact" or "little do they know," and often appears in opinion pieces and essays.
朝食を抜けばやせると思っている人が多いが、実はかえって太りやすいのだ。: Many people think skipping breakfast helps them lose weight, but in fact it makes them more likely to gain weight.
前半には「以为」「觉得」「认为」などで示す思い込みが来るのが典型で、「殊不知」の: Typically the first half states a belief with 「以为」, 「觉得」 or 「认为」, and what follows 「殊不知」 is a fact that contradicts it. In conversation, you can rephrase it with 「其实」 ("actually").
「彼は自分が正しいと思っているが、実は大きな間違いをしている。」他以为自己是对的: "He thinks he's right, but in fact he's made a big mistake." 「他以为自己是对的，___他犯了一个大错误。」
思い込みの後で実際の事実を示すのは「殊不知」。: The word that introduces the real fact after a mistaken belief is 「殊不知」.
「殊不知」の前後の関係として正しいのは？: What is the relationship between the parts before and after 「殊不知」?
前に原因、後に結果: a cause first, then the result
前に例、後にさらに極端な例: an example first, then a more extreme one
前に条件、後に目的: a condition first, then a purpose
前に思い込み、後に実際の事実: a belief first, then the actual fact
「殊不知」は思い込みと事実の食い違いを示します。: 「殊不知」 shows the gap between a belief and the facts.
「大不了」最悪でも〜すればいい: 「大不了」: at worst, if worst comes to worst
「大不了」は「最悪の場合でも〜すればいいだけだ」と、起こりうる最悪の結果を想定し: 「大不了」 is a colloquial adverb meaning "at worst, we'll just ...". It imagines the worst possible outcome and shrugs it off as no big deal, as in 「大不了再来一次」 ("at worst, we'll just do it again"). 「没什么大不了的」 is a set phrase meaning "it's no big deal."
怖がらないで。最悪、一からやり直せばいい。: Don't be afraid. At worst, we'll just start over.
「大不了」は不安な相手を励ましたり、自分の覚悟を示したりするときによく使います。: 「大不了」 is often used to reassure someone who is worried or to show you're ready for anything. Its 「了」 is read liǎo.
「間に合わなくても、最悪次の電車に乗ればいい。」赶不上也没事，___坐下一班车。: "It's fine if we miss it. At worst, we'll take the next train." 「赶不上也没事，___坐下一班车。」
「这有什么大不了的？」の意味は？: What does 「这有什么大不了的？」 mean?
反語の形で「何がそんなに大変なのか＝大したことはない」となります。: As a rhetorical question, it means "what's so terrible about it?", i.e., it's no big deal.
「未尝不…」〜でないこともない: 「未尝不…」: could well be, not out of the question
「未尝」はもともと「まだ〜したことがない」という意味の書き言葉ですが、現代では「: 「未尝」 originally means "never (yet)" in written language, but today it is mostly used as 「未尝不…」, a modest affirmative meaning "it's not that ... isn't" or "it could be said that ...". 「未尝不可」 ("there's nothing wrong with it, why not") is a set phrase. It resembles the rhetorical 「何尝」 (see the 「何尝」 entry), but 「未尝不」 gently admits a possibility.
見方を変えれば、これも良いことと言えなくもない。: Looked at from another angle, this could well be a good thing.
「未尝不」は二重否定で、意味は控えめな肯定です。「未尝不可」は提案に同意するとき: 「未尝不」 is a double negative with a modest affirmative meaning. 「未尝不可」 is handy for agreeing to a suggestion, often as 「也未尝不可」 ("that could work too").
「こう考えるのも悪くない。」这样想也___。: "Thinking of it this way isn't bad either." 「这样想也___。」
「〜してもかまわない・悪くない」は「未尝不可」。: "There's nothing wrong with it" is 「未尝不可」.
「这未尝不是一个办法。」の意味は？: What does 「这未尝不是一个办法。」 mean?
これも一つの方法と言えなくもない。: This could well be one way to do it.
これはまだ試したことのない方法だ。: This is a method we've never tried.
「未尝不」は二重否定で、控えめに「〜とも言える」と認めます。: 「未尝不」 is a double negative that modestly admits "it could be ...".
「于」は書き言葉の介詞で、話し言葉の「在」「对」「比」などに当たります。「位于」: 「于」 is a written preposition that corresponds to spoken 「在」, 「对」, 「比」 and others. It most often attaches after a verb or adjective, as in 「位于」 ("be located in"), 「出生于」 ("be born in"), 「有利于」 ("be good for") and 「大于」 ("be greater than"). 「于」 + a time can also mark when something happened. You will see it constantly in newspapers, explanatory texts and official documents.
この都市は中国南部に位置している。: This city is located in southern China.
「比去年高」は「高于去年」、「对身体有利」は「有利于身体」のように、話し言葉の介: Spoken prepositional phrases turn into "verb/adjective + 「于」": 「比去年高」 becomes 「高于去年」, and 「对身体有利」 becomes 「有利于身体」.
「この会社は北京にある。」这家公司___北京。: "This company is located in Beijing." 「这家公司___北京。」
「去年より低い」を書き言葉で言うと？: How do you say "lower than last year" in written style?
形容詞＋「于」＋比較の対象の語順です。: The order is adjective + 「于」 + the thing compared.
